label: Early original-phase step after a prefix made mostly of s/l/v/y/w
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at steps t=1-4 (t=2 alone holds 57% of the mass). It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or during copy (14 of 12.8k dev activations). It needs the earlier inputs to be mostly from {s,l,v,y,w}: those tokens dominate prev_tok, prev2_tok and first_tok (rate lifts of 4-7x). When both of the previous two inputs are in the set, precision reaches 0.72. Typical top examples are s s 0, l l s 0 and s w s 0. Among current tokens, 0, q, g, s and z (and to a lesser degree i, l, b) have the highest firing rates (about 3x lift). Adding that current-token condition raises dev F1 to 0.49 but drops mass recall to 0.54, so the unit acts like a graded sum over the prefix and current token rather than a clean boolean. Firing becomes rarer as digits in the sequence increase, and it is weaker on repeated tokens (in_first=0). The predicate captures about 94% of activation mass on dev but precision is only about 0.2: many early steps after s/l/v/y/w prefixes do not fire.
